- When sentiment is bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism; especially after recent auction supply events.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., 89.06 → 90+), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast growth to 0.5–1.0% per day post-spike.
- If official event net supply is high (e.g., >20 events/30d, supply_net > 20), model overestimates price; apply downward bias of 1–3% to forecast mean.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model is flat or rising, model underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment to forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon after volatility spikes; if true outcome drops >5% from 30d high, forecast should adjust downward by 1–2% per day for next 5 days.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment shifts in early days of event window; if sentiment turns bullish after 3–5 days, adjust forecast upward by 0.2–0.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
